title: Officer shaken after Vanderhoof shooting
article: Police now know the identity of the man fatally shot by a Vanderhoof RCMP officer early Sunday morning after an attempted break-and-enter.
Dead is Kevin Edmond St. Arnaud, a 29-year-old Vanderhoof resident .
The death is now under investigation by the North District Major Crimes Unit, while the officer is at home on regular days off.

"Like anyone would be, he was shaken by the incident," said Const. Mike Caira, on-scene in Vanderhoof. "He is certainly going to be provided with the Members' Assistance Program, which provides personal and emotional support and counselling after any traumatic incident."
It is not yet disclosed what the immediate course of action will be regarding the officer, whose name has not been released.

The officer, who has been with the RCMP since 2002, was not injured in the altercation. He was one of two Vanderhoof members who attended a late-night alarm at the Rexall Pharmacy at the Vanderhoof Co-op Mall.
They observed a suspect run from the rear of the building and the officer gave chase first in a police vehicle, then on foot.

The chase led them across the parking lot and bordering street, between buildings, across a small field and ended several hundred yards from the pharmacy when police say the suspect turned and advanced on the officer "in a threatening manner."
Police say the officer directed the suspect to cease his threatening behaviour and when that instruction was disregarded, he fired three shots, killing the suspect.

"All we know and, can discuss at this time, is he was acting in a threatening manner towards the officer, that he also refused to comply with the officer's directions and anything further is not coming out at this time, it is part of the investigation," Caira said. "During the forensic examination of the scene, stolen property from the Rexall Pharmacy and three (bullet) casings were recovered. At this time, no other weapons have been located at the scene or on the deceased."
According to Caira, cases of an RCMP officer fatally shooting a suspect are rare anywhere in Canada.

"Has this happened in Vanderhoof before?" Caira asked of those in the Vanderhoof detachment. "Everyone is shaking their heads. They say an officer here was shot and wounded in the late '80s, but no one recalls a fatal shooting involving a suspect. In Prince George there was one in about 1988. You have to go back a long time. And anytime a member's weapon is discharged, there will be a follow-up investigation, pretty much automatically."

Caira explains that RCMP standard training is for officers to always aim at the centre of mass -- the chest -- when forced to shoot at a suspect. The only exception, he says, is specialized firearms training for Emergency Response Team snipers.
An autopsy will be performed today on St. Arnaud, and the B.C. coroner's service is involved in the investigation to determine if an inquest is appropriate.
